title: Request Flow & Load Balancing
summary: See how routing, finite workers, and queues combine to determine response time.
outcomes: Separate queue time from service time in an end-to-end request.
Compare round-robin and least-outstanding routing under stated assumptions.
Explain why load balancing cannot create service capacity.

title: Capacity Estimation
summary: Turn product assumptions into transparent ranges for traffic, storage, bandwidth, and concurrent work.
outcomes: Convert daily usage into average and peak request rates with explicit units.
Estimate retained data, response bandwidth, and mean concurrency from stated assumptions.
Explain uncertainty, exclusions, and the difference between an estimate and measured capacity.

title: Distributed Rate Limiter
summary: Control bursts and protect shared capacity while making counter scope, overshoot, and failure policy explicit.
outcomes: Compare fixed-window and token-bucket decisions for the same request schedule.
Explain and calculate overshoot from independent per-node counters.
Choose an enforcement scope and backend-failure policy for a concrete operation.

title: Cache-Aside
summary: Understand cache hits, misses, TTL expiry, stale data, and origin load through a deterministic cache-aside simulation.
outcomes: Trace a GET through cache lookup, origin read, and cache fill with explicit latencies.
Explain why an origin update does not invalidate a cached entry under cache-aside.
Identify stale reads, cold-start bursts, and the effect of cache or origin unavailability.

title: URL Shortener Design Workshop
summary: Define a short-link service's requirements, estimate its demand, and defend create/redirect contracts before choosing storage and architecture.
outcomes: Separate required behavior from assumptions, non-goals and correctness constraints.
Calculate demand and data growth, then explain how changing one assumption affects the design.
Defend bounded create retries, redirect caching, expiry and error behavior.
